title: Number of Strings Which Can Be Rearranged to Contain Substring
summary: Given an integer n, determine the count of all possible strings of length n that can be rearranged to include the substring 'leet'.
statement: Given an integer n, determine the count of all possible strings of length n that can be rearranged to include the substring 'leet'. Since the result can be large, provide the answer modulo 10^9 + 7. A substring is a continuous segment of characters within a string.
constraints: Count lowercase strings whose multiset contains at least one l, two e characters, and one t, allowing rearrangement to contain leet.
hints: Only capped counts of l, e, and t matter; every other letter shares one transition.
Track an eight-ish state space with l and t capped at one and e capped at two.
For each position, add transitions for 23 other letters, l, e, and t modulo the limit.
The capped state records exactly whether the final multiset meets each requirement, and grouping the irrelevant letters preserves their multiplicity.
editorial: The capped state records exactly whether the final multiset meets each requirement, and grouping the irrelevant letters preserves their multiplicity.

tests.explanation: Exactly the twelve distinct permutations of the multiset e,e,l,t qualify.
